topic: Room: entities, DAOs, relations, migrations & Flow

questions.question: When does this Flow emit again?
questions.code:
@Query("SELECT * FROM user WHERE active = 1")
fun observeActiveUsers(): Flow<List<User>>
options: After any write to the user table, even if these rows didn't change
Only when the rows returned by this exact query differ from the last ones
Never: it emits once, and the query must be called again to get new rows
Each time the app returns to the foreground and the database is reopened
questions.explanation: Room tracks invalidation per table, not per row or query result, so any insert, update or delete in `user` re-runs the query and emits. That can produce duplicate lists, which is why `distinctUntilChanged()` is often added. It is a live stream for as long as it is collected, not a one-shot.

questions.question: By default Room throws if you run a blocking query on the main thread, unless the database was built with `allowMainThreadQueries()`.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Room checks the thread for synchronous DAO calls and throws `IllegalStateException` on the main thread, because disk I/O there causes jank and ANRs. `suspend` DAO functions and `Flow` queries avoid the problem because Room moves the work to its own executor.

questions.question: Which DAO functions are safe to call from a coroutine running on `Dispatchers.Main`? Select all that apply.
options: `suspend fun insert(user: User)`
`fun observe(): Flow<List<User>>`, then collect it
`fun getAll(): List<User>`
`fun insertNow(user: User)` (not suspend)
questions.explanation: For `suspend` and `Flow` DAO functions, Room's generated code runs the query on its own background executor, so callers on Main are not blocked. Plain blocking functions run on the caller's thread, which Room rejects on Main. Those need a background dispatcher or should be made `suspend`.

questions.question: `@PrimaryKey(autoGenerate = true) val id: Long = 0`. You insert `Note(id = 0, text = "hi")` twice. What ends up in the table?
options: Two rows with new ids, because 0 is treated as "no id set"
One row with id 0, replaced by the second insert of the note
A crash on the second insert, because id 0 is already taken
Two rows that both have id 0, since the key is not checked
questions.explanation: With `autoGenerate`, Room treats 0 (or null) as not set and lets SQLite assign the next rowid, so each insert gets a new id. That is why the default value is 0. A primary key is always unique, so two rows with the same id are impossible.

questions.question: You add a column to an entity and bump the database version from 1 to 2, without a Migration, AutoMigration or destructive fallback. What happens on a device that has version 1?
options: The app crashes when the database opens: there's no path from version 1 to 2
Room adds the new column on its own, using the entity's default value for it
Room quietly deletes and recreates the database, losing all of the old data
The build fails, because KSP can see that the schema changed without a migration
questions.explanation: Room needs an explicit path between versions; without one it throws `IllegalStateException` when the database is first opened. It never alters tables unless you declare a Migration or AutoMigration, and data is only wiped if you opt in with `fallbackToDestructiveMigration()`. The build cannot know which versions already exist on devices, so it does not fail.

questions.question: Why does this DAO method need `@Transaction`?
options: Room runs separate queries for users and playlists; the transaction keeps them consistent
@Relation compiles to a SQL JOIN, and SQLite only allows JOIN statements inside a transaction
@Transaction moves the query onto a background thread, which a List return type requires
Every DAO query that returns a List needs @Transaction or Room refuses to generate code
questions.explanation: Room loads `@Relation` data with separate queries: first the parents, then the children for those parent ids. Without a transaction, a write between those queries could pair users with inconsistent playlists, and Room warns about it at compile time. It does not use a JOIN, and `@Transaction` has nothing to do with threading.

questions.question: Which statements about Room migrations are true? Select all that apply.
options: Exporting the schema (exportSchema with a schema location) is needed for AutoMigrations and MigrationTestHelper
An AutoMigration needs an AutoMigrationSpec when you rename or delete a column or table
fallbackToDestructiveMigration() keeps the users' data and only resets the version number
After migrating, Room checks the resulting schema against the entities and throws on mismatch
questions.explanation: AutoMigrations and `MigrationTestHelper` compare the exported JSON schemas, so exporting is required. Renames and deletions are ambiguous (a rename looks like a drop plus an add), so you describe them with an `AutoMigrationSpec`. Room validates the migrated schema and throws if it does not match; the destructive fallback, as its name says, drops all data.

questions.question: `Playlist` has a foreign key to `User` with `onDelete = CASCADE`. After this call updates an existing user, all of that user's playlists are gone. Why?
options: REPLACE deletes the conflicting row and inserts a new one, so the cascade deletes the children
REPLACE turns off foreign key checks for the transaction, so the child rows become orphaned
Room runs the insert in a batch, and SQLite removes the playlists afterwards during a vacuum
The Flow briefly emits an empty list after the write, but the playlists are still in the table
questions.explanation: SQLite's `REPLACE` resolves a conflict by deleting the existing row and inserting a new one, and that delete fires `ON DELETE CASCADE`. Use `@Upsert` (Room 2.5+) or `@Update`, which update the row in place and leave children alone. The data really is deleted; it is not a display glitch.

questions.question: A `@Query` returning `Flow<User?>` for a single row emits `null` when no row matches, instead of never emitting.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Room runs the query when collection starts and emits its result, which is `null` for a nullable single-row return type with no match. It emits again after each change to the table, so the UI can show the user once the row is inserted.

questions.question: A repository must debit one account and credit another as one atomic operation, using two DAO calls. What should it use?
options: db.withTransaction { } around both, or a @Transaction DAO method calling both
coroutineScope { } with a launch for each call, so that they both finish together
A @Transaction annotation on the repository function that performs the two calls
A Mutex around the two calls, so that no other coroutine can run them at once
questions.explanation: `withTransaction` (room-ktx) runs suspending DAO calls in a single database transaction, rolling both back if either throws; a `@Transaction` method in the DAO does the same. Room only processes `@Transaction` on DAO methods, so on a repository it does nothing. A `Mutex` serializes callers, but a failure after the debit still leaves the data half-written.
